pages.b: Home / The Division 2 / Patches / Red Moon Rising The Division 2 / Y8S3.1 Update Division 2 Y8S3.1 Red Moon Rising Update Guide Title Update Y8S3.1 landed on September 23, 2026 with the Red Moon Rising event, two new exotics, the Rage Harvest return, multiplier weeks and a PvP balance pass. Our plain-language summary below — full texts live on Ubisoft's news hub . Last updated: September 24, 2026 · Covers TUY8S3.1 launch Unofficial fan summary. Game content belongs to Ubisoft; full texts linked above. Red Moon Rising Event A red moon has risen over the Dark Zone and Black Tusk have taken control. Agents entering the PvE Dark Zone face Black Tusk forces while strange alterations hit their SHD tech. The longer you stay inside, the more Red Moon Stacks you build: a mix of strong buffs and dangerous drawbacks that grows with your count. The buildup only lasts as long as the run — dying, leaving the PvE Dark Zone, or securing contaminated loot wipes the stacks, while safehouses pause the accumulation until you step back out. The event runs September 24 through November 3. New Loot Vertigo (Exotic GR9) Startling talent: suppressed enemies take Disorient, and you and allies gain +30% damage to targets out of cover for 15s. Rolls with +15% crit chance optics, +50 round magazine, +15% reload underbarrel and +10% rate of fire muzzle. Sarru (Exotic Backpack) Decoy King talent: in combat the moon cycles 8 phases every 5 seconds, amplifying all your damage from 5% up to 25% at full moon, then winding back down. A full-moon Decoy gains Overcharge and pauses the cycle for 10s. Reward Pools Dedicated Red Moon pools with exotics, Dark Zone named items, curated named items and Prototype gear. Rage Harvest Returns Rage Harvest is back from September 29 through October 6. Enemies carry Overheal protection that makes them tougher the more it stacks — break through it to build your own Rage, raising weapon damage, RPM, handling, crit chance and crit damage. The longer you keep pressure on, the longer the Rage lasts. Multiplier Weeks Dark Zone Surge (Sep 22 - 29) 3x Dark Zone XP, no DZ XP loss on death before the level cap, 2x DZ Funds. Deadeye Overdrive (Sep 29 - Oct 6) +60% headshot damage, +30% weapon damage, +40% accuracy, stability and weakpoint damage. Countdown Surge (Oct 6 - 13) Double Countdown requisition earnings. PvP & Modifier Updates Another PvP balance round covers Prototype Augments, gear and brand set bonuses, talents, exotics and SHD skills, with dedicated tuning for Vertigo and Sarru. On the modifier side, Modular Plates were reworked into steady active and passive shield regeneration, and the Signed, Shield, Delivered modifier now also refills the equipped weapon's magazine for free. What This Means for Builds Suppression and decoy playstyles gained real payoffs — test Vertigo pairings and full-moon Decoy timing in the build planner , and farm the event pools during Dark Zone Surge . FAQ When does Red Moon Rising run? Red Moon Rising runs from September 24 through November 3 in the PvE Dark Zone, overlapping the Rage Harvest return and multiplier weeks. What are the new Y8S3.1 exotics? Vertigo, an exotic GR9 with the Startling talent, and Sarru, an exotic backpack with the Decoy King talent. Both drop from Red Moon Rising reward pools. When does Rage Harvest return? Rage Harvest returns from September 29 through October 6, alongside the Deadeye Overdrive multiplier week. The daily reset happens every day at 08:00 UTC (04:00 EDT in summer). Targeted loot, daily projects and related rotations refresh at that time. When is The Division 2 weekly reset? The weekly reset happens on Tuesdays around 08:00 UTC. Vendor stock, weekly projects, invasions and legendary rotations refresh together. Tuesday maintenance can shift the exact minute, so check the server status tracker on reset day. When does the Division 2 incursion key chest reset? pages.t: Division 2 Matchmaking Goes Wrong: Broken Rain [2026]
pages.d: Twenty minutes in the Broken Rain matchmaking queue for a teammate who says nothing and rage quits on Iris. Division 2 matchmaking at its finest.
pages.b: Home / The Division 2 / Incursions & Raids / Division 2 Matchmaking Goes Horribly Wrong incursion / matchmaking Division 2 Matchmaking Goes Wrong: Broken Rain [2026] Twenty minutes in the Broken Rain matchmaking queue for a teammate who says nothing and rage quits on Iris. Division 2 matchmaking at its finest. Play video Watch Division 2 Matchmaking Goes Wrong: Broken Rain [2026] on YouTube Video Summary Part 1 of a mini-series on Division 2 matchmaking — the negative side. Twenty minutes in the Broken Rain queue, a silent random teammate (flatdriver_PL), Lester and Dwayne cleared despite the chaos, and Iris attempts that end in a rage quit because the Negotiator's Dilemma cheese has been patched. Sheriff + Striker DPS all the way. Part 2 will show a run where matchmaking actually goes right. Division 2 Incursions and Raids hub Guide Facts Mission Broken Rain Incursion (Steel Creek Dam) Content type incursion / matchmaking Difficulty/variant Random Matchmaking Duration 30:21 Published 2026-08-30 Page last checked 2026-08-30 YouTube Watch on YouTube Broken Rain Matchmaking — What Went Wrong The Queue 20 minutes waiting in the Broken Rain matchmaking queue on a Saturday afternoon. Crossplay is on, but nobody shows up. When flatdriver_PL finally joins, he says nothing — no hi, no ready check, just runs straight into the mission. Lester & Dwayne Despite the silent teammate, Lester and Dwayne go down. It's messy — everyone dies at least once — but it's a clear. flatdriver_PL swaps to a healing set for Dwayne, showing he's not completely lost. Iris — The Breaking Point The Negotiator's Dilemma Iris cheese has been patched. Now you have to do the actual EMP turbine mechanic. With a random who won't communicate, this is where it falls apart. hybrid (the healer) keeps the hive in the control room trying to heal from range instead of giving it to the player who needs it. First attempt is one EMP window away from success. Second attempt — hybrid rage quits. The Verdict 20 minutes in queue for the privilege of maybe getting a good teammate. Instead you get a silent coin flip. This is exactly why people give up on matchmaking for certain content. Open the Division 2 Incursions and Raids hub FAQ What happens in this Division 2 matchmaking video? Twenty minutes in the Broken Rain matchmaking queue, a silent random teammate (flatdriver_PL), Lester and Dwayne cleared, and Iris attempts that end in a rage quit because the Negotiator's Dilemma cheese was patched. How long is the matchmaking queue in the video? 20 minutes waiting in the Broken Rain matchmaking queue before a teammate finally joins. Why did the teammate rage quit? The Iris encounter requires coordinated EMP mechanic timing. The random teammate refused to communicate, ran a tank build without discussion, and eventually rage quit after failed attempts. What build is used in the video? Sheriff + Striker DPS setup. The random teammate switched between healing and tank builds without communicating. Is this Part 1 of a series? Yes. This is the negative side of Division 2 matchmaking. Part 2 will show a run where matchmaking actually goes right. pages.t: 5 Games Like Destiny 2 Worth Trying in 2026
pages.d: Looking for games like Destiny 2 in 2026? Five loot shooters with daily rotations, endgame builds, and co-op worth your time — including The Division 2.
pages.b: Home / Guides / Games Like Destiny 2 Guides / Loot Shooters 5 Games Like Destiny 2 Worth Trying in 2026 Destiny 2 has dominated the loot shooter space for years, but the genre has evolved. Whether you burned out on the seasonal grind, want something with a different endgame loop, or just need a break between raids, there are several strong alternatives in 2026 that scratch the same itch — daily rotations, build crafting, co-op endgame, and that satisfying loot chase. Last updated: September 17, 2026 1. The Division 2 — The Closest DNA Match Platform: PC, PlayStation, Xbox | Best for: Players who want Destiny's loot loop with a grounded, tactical twist If Destiny 2 is a sci-fi power fantasy, The Division 2 is its military-realism cousin. Same DNA — daily loot rotations, build optimization, endgame missions — but set in a post-pandemic Washington D.C. with cover-based shooting and a more methodical pace. Why it scratches the same itch Daily targeted loot rotation — Every day at 08:00 UTC, the game rotates which mission areas drop which gear brands. This is the same "check today's loot before you play" habit Destiny players already have. Endgame builds that matter — Tipping Scales, Whiplash, Striker, Regulus headshot builds — the build depth rivals Destiny's subclass customization, but with gear sets and brand bonuses instead of abilities. Escalation mode — Division 2's Tier 10 Escalation is the closest thing to Destiny's Nightfall system: scaled difficulty, matchmaking, and targeted rewards. Solo clears are possible but demand a real build. Incursions and raids — Broken Rain and Paradise Lost are Division 2's equivalent to Destiny's raids. Full squad coordination, boss mechanics, and day-one blind clears are very much a thing. Dark Zone PvP — Unlike Destiny's Crucible, the Dark Zone is a PvPvE extraction zone. High risk, high reward, and completely optional if PvP isn't your thing. What's different Division 2 is grounded and realistic where Destiny is fantastical. No space magic, no supers — just guns, gear, and positioning. The loot chase is less about chasing a single god-roll weapon and more about building synergy across gear sets, brand bonuses, and talents. Where to start Check the Division 2 loot today hub for today's targeted loot snapshot, or browse the build maker tool to theorycraft before you farm. If you want to see what endgame looks like, the Tier 10 Escalation guides show real clears with real builds. 2. Diablo 4 — The ARPG Pivot Platform: PC, PlayStation, Xbox | Best for: Players who want the loot chase with a completely different gameplay loop Diablo 4 isn't a shooter, but it shares Destiny's core loop: kill enemies, collect loot, optimize builds, repeat. The difference is isometric and real-time instead of first-person and tactical. Why it works as a Destiny alternative Helltide events — Hourly world events with dense enemy spawns and chest farming. Think of them as Destiny's public events but more frequent and more rewarding. World bosses — Every 3.5 hours, a world boss spawns with a 15-minute kill window. Group up or miss it. The same "be there at the right time" pressure Destiny has with rotating activities. Build depth — Paragon boards, aspects, uniques — Diablo 4's build system is deeper than Destiny's in raw complexity, though less visually satisfying. Seasonal content — Each season adds new mechanics, uniques, and endgame systems. The seasonal model is similar to Destiny's, just with a darker tone. What's different No PvP (unless you count the PvP zones), no raids in the traditional sense, and the endgame is more about pushing Nightmare Dungeons and The Pit than coordinating six-player encounters. It's a solo-friendly loot chase with optional group play. 3. Warframe — The Free Alternative Platform: PC, PlayStation, Xbox, Nintendo Switch | Best for: Players who want Destiny's scope without the price tag Warframe has been around for over a decade, but it's still one of the best free-to-play loot shooters available. The learning curve is steep, but the ceiling is enormous. Why it competes with Destiny Daily Sorties — Three mission modifiers with rotating rewards. Similar to Destiny's daily challenges but with more variety in objectives. Arbitrations — High-difficulty endless missions with exclusive rewards. The closest Warframe gets to Destiny's Grandmaster Nightfalls. Build variety — Warframes are essentially Destiny subclasses made flesh. Each one has unique abilities, and modding them is where the real depth lives. Trading economy — Unlike Destiny, Warframe has a player-driven trading system. You can earn premium currency (Platinum) by selling mods and parts to other players. Massive content library — Years of updates mean there's more content than any new player can digest in a month. It's overwhelming, but in a good way. What's different Warframe is faster. Much faster. If Destiny is a tactical shooter, Warframe is a movement-based power fantasy. You're bullet-jumping through tilesets at speeds that make Destiny's sprint feel slow. The aesthetic is also more sci-fi anime than military realism. 4. The First Descendant — The Newcomer Platform: PC, PlayStation, Xbox | Best for: Players who want Destiny's visual polish with a fresh coat of paint The First Descendant launched in 2024 and has been steadily improving. It's free-to-play, visually stunning, and borrows heavily from both Destiny and Warframe — which isn't necessarily a bad thing. Why it's worth watching Raid-style operations — Four-player co-op missions with boss mechanics that feel like Destiny's raids, just smaller in scale. Character-based system — Like Warframe's Frames or Destiny's subclasses, each Descendant has unique abilities. The difference is you're unlocking and leveling individual characters, not just gear. Visual fidelity — Built on Unreal Engine 5, it's one of the best-looking loot shooters available. If visual polish matters to you, this is the prettiest option on the list. Regular updates — New Descendants, weapons, and content drops keep the game evolving. The developers are actively responding to community feedback. What's different It's newer and less polished than Destiny. The endgame is shallower, the content library is smaller, and the balance is still being tuned. But if you're tired of Destiny's formula and want something fresh, The First Descendant is the most visually impressive alternative right now. 5. Remnant 2 — The Co-op Shooter With Soul Platform: PC, PlayStation, Xbox | Best for: Players who want Destiny's co-op shooting with roguelike variety Remnant 2 isn't a live-service game, but it's one of the best co-op loot shooters released in recent years. Think Destiny meets Dark Souls with procedurally generated worlds. Why it deserves a spot Procedural layouts — Each playthrough remixes world layouts, boss encounters, and loot drops. No two runs are identical, which keeps the replay value high. Build crafting — Dual-class archetypes, mutators, and ring combinations create genuine build diversity. Some builds feel as broken as Destiny's strongest loadouts. Co-op focused — Designed for 1-3 players from the ground up. No forced matchmaking, no randoms — just you and your squad. Boss fights — Some of the best boss design in the genre. Each encounter has unique mechanics that demand adaptation, not just DPS checks. What's different It's not a live service. There's no daily reset, no seasonal content, no FOMO. You play it, you beat it, you move on — or you come back for the DLC. It's Destiny's gameplay loop distilled into a finite experience, which some players prefer. Quick Comparison Game Daily Resets Build Depth PvP Co-op Price The Division 2 ✅ Loot + server status High ✅ Dark Zone ✅ Full $30 (often on sale) Diablo 4 ✅ Helltide + world bosses Very High ⚠️ Limited ✅ Full $70 + expansions Warframe ✅ Sorties + Arbitrations Very High ✅ Conclave ✅ Full Free The First Descendant ⚠️ Some rotations Medium ❌ None ✅ Full Free Remnant 2 ❌ None High ❌ None ✅ Full $40 The Verdict If you want the closest thing to Destiny 2 in 2026, The Division 2 is the answer. Same daily loot rotation habit, same build-crafting depth, same endgame raid structure — just with a different setting and a more tactical feel. The community is active, the guides are detailed, and the game respects your time more than it used to. If you want something completely different, Diablo 4 or Remnant 2 break the mold. If you want free, Warframe is still king. And if you want pretty graphics and a fresh start, The First Descendant is worth watching. The loot shooter genre is in a good place right now. There's no reason to stick with one game when the grass is genuinely greener on the other side. First Schaeffer, then Lewis and Wally. Imagine my surprise when I discovered you even managed to recruit Vik. I thought you hated him after what happened at Odea, but here you are, welcoming old enemies into your house and giving them the literal keys to the Castle. I haven't decided if you're a genius with boundless empathy or a moron who actually believes that people can change. People don't change. Most of the time, if you think someone has changed it's because you never really saw them. You never look close enough to see if the person staring back at you is genuine or is hiding their true intentions. That's why you're so easy to fool. And why I will always be two steps ahead of you. Connection not applicable Continuity division game universe Canon scope game canon Verification draft Reviewed 2026-08-19 Georgetown Shay Montgomery talks about Victor Tranh and how Georgetown was exposed to DC-62 Features SHAY MONTGOMERY. Contains 1 dialogue exchanges. [1] That's where Victor Tranh came in. Professor Tranh was a big deal in neighborhood politics, and it didn't take much for him to convince people that the right thing to do was evict the patients and spray the neighborhood. It would make all of them safe, he promised. Now I knew this was bullshit - they hadn't had any time to run tests on this DC-62 stuff he was talking about - and I said so. Loudly. And that's when Victor Tranh lied. He told people I was sick, too, which I wasn't, at least not yet. He had me kicked out with the rest of the infected. Sent us to the CERA camp down by the river and sprayed his DC-62. I hear it killed him. Justice, she works in funny ways. [1] Refugee Camp Shay Montgomery talks about her experience in a CERA camp run by True Sons Features SHAY MONTGOMERY. Contains 1 dialogue exchanges. [1] Purpose Shay Montgomery talks about why she escaped the camp Features SHAY MONTGOMERY. Contains 1 dialogue exchanges. [1] Making a Difference Shay Montgomery talks about a family she helped after escaping the camps Features SHAY MONTGOMERY. Contains 1 dialogue exchanges. [1] I could tell that story about twenty different families around the city, and all those stories would be true. I'm not bragging. I'm asking you what you're doing to make a difference, and if you're just surviving, to think about doing a little more than that. [1] Reflective Shay Montgomery reflects on her life before the lockdown and how far she has come Features SHAY MONTGOMERY. Contains 1 dialogue exchanges. [1] I don't even know if anyone else who was at that party is still alive. And yet here I am, about to breach the Capital Station Dark Zone again, looking for meds for the people who've fallen through the cracks of whatever system's left. I like to think I'm doing the right thing. [1] Capital Station Shay Montgomery talks about the events that led to Capitol Station being abandoned Features SHAY MONTGOMERY. Contains 1 dialogue exchanges. [1] I'm more interested in what got left at the field hospital. There's still meds there, still sterile equipment and surgical supplies. Hell, there's even clean toilet paper. I've been in there three times and haven't come close to cleaning it out. I worry 'm getting predictable. But so far, it's been worth the risk. [1] Orphans Shay Montgomery talks about a little boy she plans on resettling at the Theater Features SHAY MONTGOMERY. Contains 1 dialogue exchanges. [1] Haunted Shay Montgomery talks about going back to the CERA camp in DZ South Features SHAY MONTGOMERY. Contains 1 dialogue exchanges. [1] Shit. Got DC-62 on my shoes. That'll have to come off. Not the first time, though. Won't be the last. pages.t: Copyright and Quotation Policy | Raigulus Lore
pages.d: The archive publishes original, source-led analysis and evidence locators, never copied editions, scripts, scans, panels or book excerpts.
pages.b: Copyright and Quotation Policy | Raigulus Lore Raigulus Division 2 Builds Build Maker Loot Server Status Patches Missions Escalation Dark Zone Manhunts Bosses Incursions & Raids PvP Lore About Discord YouTube Home / Lore / Copyright and Quotation Policy Publication boundary Copyright and Quotation Policy The archive publishes original, source-led analysis and evidence locators, never copied editions, scripts, scans, panels or book excerpts. Public pages use original expression Public pages may publish identifying metadata, independently written summaries, factual lore points, relationship maps and source links. Transmedia records do not publish dialogue, captions, OCR text, translated excerpts, chapter-by-chapter or page-by-page retellings, panels, cover art, scans or downloaded editions. There is no automatic safe word count or percentage for copying another work. When a source is a book, comic or other expressive work, the archive's default is no verbatim quotation and no visual reproduction unless a separate rights review documents permission or a narrowly necessary exception. A lore page must add original analysis rather than substitute for the source. It may identify a documented fact or high-level narrative connection, but it must not reconstruct the work's prose, scene sequence, panel sequence or other protected expression. Source and media gate Published lore claims use official publisher, developer, government, primary-record or lawfully captured direct-game sources. Unofficial mirrors, file lockers, peer-to-peer links, leaked files and access-controlled material obtained without permission are not accepted as public lore sources. A source URL may identify where a lawful public edition or official statement can be found, but it cannot point to a downloadable ebook, comic archive, transcript, raw audio, extracted game asset or credentialed/private file. Covers, logos, author photographs, comic art and promotional artwork are excluded unless the archive has a documented right to use them. Original gameplay capture is used here as an evidence locator, not as a redistributed game asset. It is never mirrored as a downloadable site file and does not itself create permission to reuse footage, music, voice or other game assets; any publication beyond the factual record must comply with the applicable publisher and platform policies. Names, titles and brand use Titles, character names and short identifying labels are used only to identify the subject of independent commentary. The archive does not imply publisher approval, reproduce publisher branding as its own, or present source material as a substitute for an official edition. Private research material Only lawfully obtained or explicitly authorized research material may be used in the private research workflow. The workflow must not use or publicize copies from unofficial mirrors, peer-to-peer services, file lockers or access controls bypassed without permission. Private research artifacts never belong in the public repository or its source registry. The repository guard rejects common raw-text, transcript, scan, ebook, download-link, credential and media fields or file formats from public lore paths. Rights-holder concerns If a rights-holder identifies a specific public page, claim or asset that may exceed this boundary, that item is removed from public publication while its source and rights basis are reviewed. A correction report should identify the exact URL and material at issue; reporters should not post private legal documents or access credentials in a public issue. Platform-level copyright notices follow the hosting platform's reporting process. This archive treats a notice as a reason to preserve the record of review, not as permission to republish the disputed material elsewhere. Also known as: Dollar Flu Connection not applicable Continuity division game universe Canon scope game canon Verification source reviewed Reviewed 2026-07-19 Outbreak and collapse Green Poison is the biological trigger for the franchise's institutional collapse. It spreads during the Black Friday period and becomes widely known as the Dollar Flu. [1] [2] Origin and reach The games identify Gordon Amherst as its creator. The crisis is centered on the United States, but official background does not describe it as exclusively American. [2] [3] Claim ledger Every factual statement below must retain at least one traceable source. confirmed Ubisoft's glossary identifies Green Poison as the Dollar Flu and links it to mass deaths, quarantine, riots and New York's collapse. [1] confirmed The franchise story recap places the Green Poison outbreak on Black Friday. [2] confirmed Virologist Gordon Amherst created Green Poison; Vitaly Tchernenko was not involved in its development. [2] confirmed Official franchise background says the United States was hit hardest but cases also emerged elsewhere in the world. pages.t: Collectible Evidence Intake | Raigulus Lore
pages.d: The capture checklist used to turn in-game collectibles, comms and recordings into reviewable lore records.
pages.b: Collectible Evidence Intake | Raigulus Lore Raigulus Division 2 Builds Build Maker Loot Server Status Patches Missions Escalation Dark Zone Manhunts Bosses Incursions & Raids PvP Lore About Discord YouTube Home / Lore / Collectible Evidence Intake Research intake Collectible Evidence Intake The capture checklist used to turn in-game collectibles, comms and recordings into reviewable lore records. Submit a collectible evidence record Required capture set Capture the in-game collection menu showing the category, item title and completion position; add the map, mission or room locator where the item is obtained; record platform, interface language and the exact game build or season. For audio, provide only a lawfully captured or authorized recording privately to the authorized research agent and list every speaker you can identify. Uncertain speakers must remain marked unknown rather than being guessed. What becomes public The public record contains identifying metadata, an original summary, key lore claims, speaker attribution confidence and precise evidence locators. Complete audio, video, subtitle dumps and working transcripts stay outside this public repository unless a separate rights review approves them. A collectible is counted as captured only after its identity and locator are evidenced. It is source-reviewed only after the media or menu capture supports every published claim, and it is published only after human approval. Duplicate and conflict handling Alternate-language or later-build captures are linked to the same collectible identity rather than counted twice. If wording, speaker labels or placement changes between builds, both observations remain versioned and the conflict is shown instead of silently overwritten. Comments Unofficial, source-led research into The Division universe and its real-world influences. Lore Archive / Methodology / Corrections / YouTube @raigulus / Feedback

pages.t: The Reborn | Raigulus Lore
pages.d: An anti-fossil-fuel extremist faction that drives Compromised's Gulf Coast refinery conflict.

Connection not applicable Continuity division transmedia Canon scope official transmedia Verification source reviewed Reviewed 2026-07-28 Conflict over the supply network The Reborn target the transport and refinery infrastructure that survivor communities rely on, presenting their campaign as a break with fossil-fuel dependence. [1] Used by rogue agents Compromised presents the faction as a manipulated actor rather than an isolated Gulf Coast force: rogue agents supply its leadership while steering the regional confrontation toward their own goals. [1] A temporary later alignment — major spoilers Hunted later places the Reborn in a temporary alignment against Black Tusk. That source-specific response does not erase the faction's earlier Gulf Coast campaign, nor does it establish a permanent alliance with the Division or the Molossi. [2] Claim ledger Every factual statement below must retain at least one traceable source. confirmed Compromised identifies the Reborn as the force attacking southern food convoys and advancing on Gulf Coast refinery communities. [1] confirmed The faction's broadcasts frame continuing fossil-fuel production as an offense that must be stopped, making the Groves refinery a primary target. [1] confirmed The novel reveals that the Reborn's leadership accepted military material from rogue agents, who used the faction as part of a wider Gulf Coast manipulation. [1] confirmed Hunted depicts the Reborn joining a temporary, source-specific alignment with the Division against Black Tusk during the Albuquerque operation. pages.t: Research Methodology | Raigulus Lore
pages.d: How the Raigulus Division Lore Archive separates evidence, canon, interpretation and uncertainty.
pages.b: Research Methodology | Raigulus Lore Raigulus Division 2 Builds Build Maker Loot Server Status Patches Missions Escalation Dark Zone Manhunts Bosses Incursions & Raids PvP Lore About Discord YouTube Home / Lore / Research Methodology Editorial standard Research Methodology How the Raigulus Division Lore Archive separates evidence, canon, interpretation and uncertainty. No source, no claim Every factual lore statement is recorded as a claim and linked to one or more registered sources. A source must support the exact scope of the claim; a related page or search snippet is not enough. Direct game captures and official publications are preferred. Community material can identify research leads, but it cannot be the only support for a published factual claim. A registered link is an evidence locator, not permission to reproduce the material behind it. Fact, fiction and comparison Real-world records, Division continuity and editorial comparison are labelled separately. Similarity is not treated as proof of influence, and contradictions remain visible rather than being resolved by guesswork. Human publication gate Automated research may reach source-reviewed status, but only a designated human editor can approve human-reviewed or published status. Review dates and unresolved notes remain attached to each record. Comments Unofficial, source-led research into The Division universe and its real-world influences. pages.d: An Operation: Crossroads protagonist whose story starts with a Division recruitment in Washington, then continues through Compromised and Hunted.

Connection not applicable Continuity division transmedia Canon scope official transmedia Verification source reviewed Reviewed 2026-07-28 Recruited origin The first Operation: Crossroads novel presents Kanhai before her Division career, in Washington's post-Green Poison recovery. Its recruitment story is official transmedia material, not a retroactive game-mission record. [1] Gulf Coast assignment Kanhai leads the novel's field cell as it follows attacks on the southern supply network toward the Texas Gulf Coast. [2] Epilogue status The book treats Kanhai's survival after the Battleship Texas operation as a major cliffhanger. The people holding her claim to be DHS, but the narrative does not verify that claim within this volume. [2] Hunted continuation — major spoilers Hunted follows the unresolved Battleship Texas cliffhanger: ISAC reports Kanhai as Rogue, while Brenda Wells pursues the evidence in the American Southwest. The novel adds a coercive Black Tusk context to Kanhai's technical work and keeps that context source-specific rather than treating it as a universal explanation for Rogue status. [3] Claim ledger Every factual statement below must retain at least one traceable source. confirmed Recruited's published premise introduces Maira Kanhai as a Washington survivor with a cybersecurity background whose earlier Maryland loss precedes her opportunity to join the Strategic Homeland Division. [1] confirmed Compromised places Maira Kanhai in charge of a Division cell sent from the Kansas Core to investigate attacks on southern food convoys and Texas refinery infrastructure. [2] confirmed The novel's epilogue reveals that Kanhai survives the Battleship Texas operation and wakes in the care of people presenting themselves as Department of Homeland Security personnel. [2] confirmed Hunted confirms that Kanhai is alive and that ISAC evidence reports her as Rogue, prompting Brenda Wells to assemble a Division cell and investigate rather than accept the status at face value. [3] confirmed In Hunted's source-specific plot, Black Tusk exploits Kanhai while she is captive and medically vulnerable, using her technical expertise against Division Core infrastructure. [3] editorial distinction Hunted adds coercion and manipulation to the context of Kanhai's Rogue status, but the work does not turn that context into a blanket exoneration or a general rule for other Rogue Agents. [1] A disposable operative The final Washington sequence makes the chain of command explicit but keeps the controlling organization insulated: Mantis is removed by Black Tusk before she can be retained as a source. [1] Earlier codename usage Broken Dawn uses the Mantis codename for a remote handler attached to Ike Ronson's operation. [1] confirmed Broken Dawn also uses Mantis as the codename for a remote handler influencing Division Agent Ike Ronson; the novel does not name that handler's organization. [2] unknown The reviewed official sources do not establish that Broken Dawn's handler and the Black Tusk operative in Extremis Malis are the same individual, so this archive keeps the codename link unresolved. Also known as: NSPD-51, HSPD-20, National Continuity Policy Connection confirmed influence Continuity real world Canon scope real world with fictional extension Verification source reviewed Reviewed 2026-07-18 What the public directive says The archived directive defines a national continuity policy, assigns coordination responsibilities and describes continuity concepts intended to preserve essential federal functions during a catastrophic emergency. [1] [2] Where The Division becomes fictional The franchise builds a fictional classified annex around the real directive and uses that invention to establish the Strategic Homeland Division. This distinction matters: continuity policy is real, while the SHD organization and its extraordinary field authority belong to The Division's fiction. [1] [2] Real world vs. The Division Topic Real world The Division Assessment Public purpose Continuity of federal government structures, operations and essential functions. The fictional legal and institutional basis for activating SHD agents after catastrophe. The game extends a real continuity policy with a fictional organization. [1] [2] Strategic Homeland Division Not established in the public directive. Presented as originating from a classified annex within the fictional setting. Explicit franchise fiction, not a real agency claim. [1] [2] Claim ledger Every factual statement below must retain at least one traceable source. confirmed NSPD-51/HSPD-20 establishes United States policy for continuity of federal government structures and operations during a catastrophic emergency. [1] confirmed President George W. Bush signed the directive on May 4, 2007; its archived public release is dated May 9, 2007. [1] [2] confirmed fictional extension The public real-world directive does not establish the Strategic Homeland Division; Ubisoft describes the SHD as a fictional classified-annex development inside The Division's universe. pages.t: Operation Dark Winter | Raigulus Lore
pages.d: A 2001 senior-level tabletop exercise built around a fictional smallpox attack, and a documented real-world influence on the premise of The Division.
pages.b: Operation Dark Winter | Raigulus Lore Raigulus Division 2 Builds Build Maker Loot Server Status Patches Missions Escalation Dark Zone Manhunts Bosses Incursions & Raids PvP Lore About Discord YouTube Home / Lore / Real-world influences / Operation Dark Winter real world event Operation Dark Winter A 2001 senior-level tabletop exercise built around a fictional smallpox attack, and a documented real-world influence on the premise of The Division. Also known as: Dark Winter Connection confirmed influence Continuity real world Canon scope real world Verification source reviewed Reviewed 2026-07-18 What happened in the real world? Dark Winter was a senior-level training exercise, not a real outbreak. Its fictional scenario tested how national leaders might respond to a deliberate smallpox attack while confronting vaccine shortages, intergovernmental coordination problems, public communication and civil-liberty questions. [1] Connection to The Division Ubisoft explicitly names Dark Winter as a real-world inspiration for The Division. The useful comparison is the stress placed on institutions during a fast-moving biological crisis. The franchise turns that policy exercise into a fictional collapsed-world narrative; it does not reproduce the exercise literally. [1] [2] Real world vs. The Division Topic Real world The Division Assessment Nature A fictional training scenario used in a real 2001 tabletop exercise. A fictional franchise in which a biological crisis causes institutional and social collapse. Documented influence, not an adaptation of the exercise scenario. [1] [2] Primary focus Government decision-making, public-health capacity, communication and continuity under pressure. Field operations and survival inside the aftermath of a catastrophic outbreak. Shared crisis framework; different purpose and narrative scale. [1] [2] Claim ledger Every factual statement below must retain at least one traceable source. confirmed Dark Winter was held on June 22–23, 2001 at Andrews Air Force Base and simulated a covert smallpox attack on the United States. [1] confirmed The exercise followed senior former officials through successive National Security Council meetings as the fictional outbreak expanded. [1] confirmed influence Ubisoft identifies Operation Dark Winter as one of the real-world events that directly inspired The Division's underlying premise. [2] editorial distinction The real exercise is an influence on the franchise, not an event inside The Division's fictional continuity. [1] [2] Related records Directive 51 (NSPD-51 / HSPD-20) co foundational influence Sources [1] Dark Winter: A Training Tabletop Exercise — Johns Hopkins Center for Health Security (undated). pages.b: The Division 2 Story Timeline | Raigulus Lore Raigulus Division 2 Builds Build Maker Loot Server Status Patches Missions Escalation Dark Zone Manhunts Bosses Incursions & Raids PvP Lore About Discord YouTube Home / Lore / Timeline The Division 2 story chronology The Division 2 Story Timeline & Lore Chronology Use this source-led Division 2 lore timeline for the Washington campaign, Year One Episodes, Warlords of New York and connected official transmedia. Exact dates are shown only when a source establishes them. Relative sequence is labelled rather than converted into invented calendar dates; same-position, sequence-only records may overlap or be grouped without asserting a fixed internal order. relative Green Poison Outbreak Black Friday — Green Poison begins the franchise crisis The Black Friday biological outbreak that breaks public order, overwhelms response systems and begins the central crisis of The Division universe.
